news.title: 7,000 Langflow servers are under attack. LangGraph and LangChain have the same holes
news.summary_raw: Your AI agent did exactly what it was designed to do. The framework underneath it just handed an attacker a shell on the box that holds your OpenAI key, your database credentials, and your CRM tokens.That is not a hypothetical. In a few months, three of the most widely deployed AI agent frameworks each turned a known, ordinary bug class into a way through. Check Point Research chained a SQL injection in LangGraph’s SQLite checkpointer to full remote code execution. Tenable and VulnCheck tracked
news.summary: 7,000 Langflow servers are under attack due to vulnerabilities in LangGraph and LangChain, allowing attackers to obtain sensitive data such as OpenAI keys and database credentials. This highlights a critical weakness in AI agent frameworks.
news.enterprise_use: Check your Langflow servers and assess the risk of using AI agent frameworks with known security vulnerabilities. Missing this means leaving your organization's sensitive data exposed. Langflow is one of the tools you use, as is Google Workspace if you use their AI integrations. Your SSO providers should be audited for similar vulnerabilities.

news.title: Beyond LoRA: Can you beat the most popular fine-tuning technique?
news.summary: Hugging Face explores the limitations of LoRA, a widely used fine-tuning technique in AI. LoRA has become a standard for efficient and effective model fine-tuning, allowing users to update a model's weights with a small, low-rank matrix. However, researchers at Hugging Face question whether it is the best approach, highlighting potential biases and limitations.
news.enterprise_use: This news is relevant in the context of potential AI model risks and limitations. IT engineers may want to revisit their model training and fine-tuning practices to ensure they stay up-to-date with the latest best practices and avoid potential biases in their AI systems.
